faq.title: Common Questions Before Visiting Clínica Hispana Cruz
faq.subtitle: What neighbors from Aldine, Greenspoint and north Houston usually ask us before their first visit
faq.q1: Is a booked time slot required, or can I just show up?
faq.a1: No booking is needed. Clínica Hispana Cruz sees patients in the order they arrive: walk into Suite D on Airline Drive, give your name at the front desk, and the clinic's medical team will call you when it's your turn. That way you can come in the day you start feeling sick instead of waiting for an open slot on a calendar.
faq.q2: No health insurance at all: will you still treat me?
faq.a2: Absolutely. The clinic runs on self-pay, so nobody asks for an insurance card, policy number or eligibility paperwork before examining you. You can ask the front desk what a specific service costs before your visit, and our promotions page lists the current packages so you can plan ahead without any surprises at checkout.
faq.q3: Will the staff understand me if I only speak Spanish?
faq.a3: Yes. From check-in to the explanation of your diagnosis, everything happens in Spanish, with no interpreter in the middle and no forms you can't follow. Relatives who would rather talk in English get their visit in English, no problem. What matters is that you leave knowing what you have, what to do at home and when to come back.
faq.q4: Which days and hours are you open?
faq.a4: We're open seven days a week, Monday through Sunday, from 9 in the morning until 9 at night. Those extended hours let you stop by before work, after your shift or on the weekend, when many other offices have already closed. On holidays, send us a WhatsApp message first to confirm the schedule hasn't changed.
faq.q5: How can I pay for my visit?
faq.a5: You can pay with cash or with a credit or debit card right at the front desk once your visit is over. We don't bill insurance companies, so no statement shows up in your mailbox weeks later. To find out what a test or procedure costs before you come in, message us on WhatsApp or check the promotions section of the website.
faq.q6: What papers and items should I have with me the first time I come?
faq.a6: Bring a photo ID and a list of the medicines you take with their doses, or simply the bottles if that's easier. If you have earlier lab results, prescriptions, or forms your school, employer or paperwork requires, bring those as well: the medical team can then review your whole history and avoid repeating tests you don't need.
faq.q7: Where in Houston is the clinic?
faq.a7: You'll find us at 7640 Airline Dr, Suite D, Houston, TX 77037, on the city's north side. We sit just off Interstate 45 and close to neighborhoods like Aldine, Greenspoint, Hidden Valley, Northline and East Aldine. If you use GPS, search for Clínica Hispana Cruz on Airline Drive and it will take you right to our door.
faq.q8: Can I get my green card medical exam done here?
faq.a8: Yes. The clinic has a USCIS-designated Civil Surgeon who performs the <link>I-693 immigration medical exam</link> required for adjustment of status. It covers the physical exam, the lab tests the agency asks for and a review of your vaccination record. Bring your passport or photo ID and any vaccine records you have so we can check which doses you still need.
faq.q9: What if I need lab work?
faq.a9: Often it can be handled during the same visit. If the medical team orders a blood, urine or stool test, the sample is collected right here, with no trip to another building and no second appointment to schedule. Once results are ready we walk you through them in plain language, and if any result calls for it, we help arrange a referral to a specialist.
faq.q10: Where do I park, and is the entrance wheelchair accessible?
faq.a10: There's free patient parking right in front of the building, so you won't need to feed a meter or pay for a separate lot. The entrance and the restrooms are accessible for people who use a wheelchair. If you're bringing a relative who needs help getting out of the car, let us know when you arrive and our staff will lend a hand.
faq.q11: I'm looking for a Latino clinic close to home in north Houston. Is Cruz a good fit?
faq.a11: If you live or work around Airline Drive, Aldine, Greenspoint or Northline, it likely is: Clínica Hispana Cruz opened in July 2023 specifically to give those families a nearby option, in their language and without an insurance requirement. We take walk-ins seven days a week, and you can text us on WhatsApp to ask about a service before you leave home.
faq.q12: Can Clínica Hispana Cruz be my family medicine home?
faq.a12: Yes. Many patients come back here for routine checkups, ongoing diabetes, blood pressure or cholesterol follow-up, seasonal flu shots and school physicals. Staying with one primary care home lets the medical team get to know your history, compare new results with earlier ones and catch changes early, before they turn into bigger problems.

location.about: Clínica Hispana Cruz is a walk-in medical clinic at 7640 Airline Dr, Suite D, Houston, TX 77037, in north Houston near I-45, Aldine and Greenspoint. It is open Monday through Sunday from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM and sees patients with or without health insurance, with self-pay by cash or card. Care is in Spanish, and the staff also speaks English. Services include family medicine, diabetes, blood pressure and cholesterol care, basic gynecology, lab work, ultrasound, DOT physicals, vaccines, wound care and the I-693 immigration medical exam with a USCIS-designated Civil Surgeon. It has free parking, a wheelchair-accessible entrance and restrooms, and WhatsApp for questions. It opened in July 2023 and is one of the four Clínica Hispana Cruz locations in Houston; the others are on Kuykendahl Rd (Cruz 2), S Braeswood Blvd (Cruz 3) and Beechnut St (Cruz 4).
